title: First 90→1000: New Hire Playbook for Scaled Impact
author: Asha Patel
content:
## Purpose
This playbook describes a reproducible new-hire experience that helps individuals move from Day 0 to independently delivering measurable impact as the company scales (target milestones: 90 days, 180 days, 12 months). It integrates working-at-Redwood norms, role & career ladder expectations, benefits orientation, hiring handoff details, and the internal tools access matrix required for day-to-day work.

## Scope and Audience
- Audience: new individual contributors (ICs) and people managers across engineering, product, and go-to-market functions.
- Scope: onboarding (pre-boarding → first year), manager and buddy responsibilities, basic benefits orientation, career ladder signposting, and required internal tool access.

## Outcomes (what success looks like)
By day 90: role-level competency demonstrated through a scoped deliverable, functioning local dev/workflow access, and a documented 30–90 plan.
By day 180: ownership of a small product/feature area or operational domain; first calibration with manager on career trajectory.
By month 12: clear leveling assessment readiness, repeated cross-functional contributions, and ownership of ownerable metrics.

## High-level timeline and priorities
1) Pre-boarding (offer → start date)
   - HR: collect bank/KYC, benefits enrollment links, and background checks (if applicable).
   - IT: create core accounts (Okta, email, Slack, Jira, Confluence), assign laptop order, and create initial infra tickets.
   - Manager: send welcome note with 1-page role context and 30/60/90 expectations.
2) Day 0–7: orientation and quick wins
   - Attend Company 101 and Security 101 sessions.
   - Complete required compliance e-learning (<= 3 days).
   - Pair with buddy to complete the 'first-commit' path: fork repository, lint, run tests, and open a tiny PR.
3) Weeks 2–6: ramp and contribution
   - Deliver a scoped bugfix or small feature.
   - Weekly 1:1 established; 30/60/90 plan refined.
4) Days 60–90: ownership and feedback
   - Present deliverable in team demo.
   - Formal 90-day check-in documented in Confluence (manager + peer feedback).
5) 3–12 months: broaden impact and development
   - Participate in at least one cross-functional project.
   - Career conversation and leveling calibration at 6 and 12 months.

## Role & Career Ladder Snapshot (quick reference)
Note: this is a condensed signpost. Full competency matrices live under /02_roles-and-career.
| Level | Typical Title | Expectations (30/90/180) | Example success signal |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| L1 | Associate IC | 30: environment set up; 90: small feature; 180: reliable completion of assigned tasks | First complete feature merged and validated in production |
| L2 | IC | 30: codebase fluency; 90: feature ownership; 180: cross-team stakeholder alignment | Leads feature with measurable metric improvement |
| L3 | Senior IC | 30: design contributions; 90: mentor others; 180: technical leadership in area | Owns roadmap slice and reduces operational toil |
| L4 | Staff / Principal | 30: influence strategy; 90: cross-team design tradeoffs; 180: long-term system impact | Drives architectural changes, measurable product velocity gains |

## Benefits & Perks Quick Orientation
- Health: medical, dental, vision (enrollment window: first 30 days).
- Time off: 20 PTO days prorated first year + national holidays; flexible parental leave (see People Ops benefits page).
- Stipends: home office ($300), learning & development ($1,200/yr).
- Financial: 401(k) matching up to 4% after 90 days.
- Wellness: mental health platform access from day 1.

Eligibility notes: equity vesting starts the first full payroll period. Benefit-specific waiting periods are listed on the People Ops benefits landing page.

## Hiring & Onboarding Handoff (recruiter → manager → team)
Checklist for recruiter at offer acceptance:
- Offer packet and benefits links sent.
- Candidate profile and accepted offer committed to ATS with start date and manager contact.
- Passport of hiring decisions (interview scorecard PDF) attached to candidate record.
Manager tasks (before start date):
1) Send role context note with: role objectives, top 3 priorities for first 90 days, suggested reading, and the buddy assignment.
2) Open onboarding Confluence page and add the new hire’s name, calendar invites, and a first-week schedule.
Team tasks (first 48 hours):
- Welcome channel message in Slack and short ‘meet & greet’ demo slot scheduled.
- Assign first small ticket with clear acceptance criteria and owner review.

## Manager & Buddy Responsibilities (concise)
Manager:
- Prepare 30/60/90 success criteria and share by Day 1.
- Schedule weekly 1:1 for first 12 weeks.
- Provide timely feedback and milestones for career calibration.
Buddy:
- Day-to-day survival guide: runbook for local dev, codebase pointers, and team norms.
- Serve as first-stop troubleshooting and cultural guide for 90 days.

## Internal Tools Access Matrix (essential items)
Represented below as a minimal table; working links and Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) templates are in the Internal Tools onboarding page.
| Tool | Purpose | Default Access (first week) | Action owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Okta | SSO & identity | Provisioned by IT | IT Ops |
| Gmail | Company email | Auto-provision | IT Ops |
| Slack | Team comms | Team channels + onboarding channel | Manager |
| Jira | Issue tracking | Developer project role | Manager/EngOps |
| Confluence | Docs & runbooks | Editor on team spaces | Manager |
| GitHub | Code | Write to forked repos; team repo access after PR review | EngOps |
| Internal CI / Build | CI visibility | Read by default; exec after approval | Eng SRE |

Access escalation: when access fails, open an IT Ops ticket (IT Slack triage channel: #it-ops) with subject: "Access request: <tool> for <name>". Aim SLA: 48 business hours for standard requests; 8 hours for urgent infra access for on-call.

## 30/60/90 Planning Template (use this to align expectations)
1) 30 days (Learn): key stakeholders met, product areas understood, basic dev environment verified.
2) 60 days (Contribute): first scoped deliverable shipped; feedback integrated.
3) 90 days (Own): owning a feature or operational workflow with measurable acceptance criteria.

Sample 30–90 objective (paste into Confluence):
- Objective: Reduce average feature cycle time for team X by 15% for minor user stories.
- 30d: Map current flow, identify top 3 bottlenecks.
- 60d: Implement fix for top bottleneck, measure cycle time.
- 90d: Iterate on follow-ups and document playbook for team.

## Career Development and Calibration
- Quarterly calibration: manager compiles evidence and growth markers; people-ops coordinates cross-team calibration cycles.
- Learning plan: use L&D stipend within first 90 days; submit course plan in Confluence for approval.
- Mentorship: pair new hires with a mentor (different from buddy) in month 2 for career coaching.

## Manager First-90 Checklist (actionable)
- Offer acceptance: confirm start logistics, send equipment request.
- Preboarding: set up accounts and add calendar invites for Company 101, Security 101, and Team Orientation.
- Day 1: share 30/60/90 doc and immediate priorities.
- Weekly: track deliverables, unblock risks, provide written feedback each 30 days.
- 90-day review: document outcome (strengths, blockers, next goals) and submit form to People Ops.

## Typical Risk & Escalation Paths
- Access delays: escalate to IT Ops manager and copy People Ops.
- Role clarity issues: immediate 1:1 + updated role brief; if unresolved, involve chapter lead.
- Performance concerns within first 90 days: follow the Performance Improvement primer (link in related pages) with People Ops involvement.

## Templates and Artifacts (appendix)
- 30/60/90 Plan template: copyable confluence template link (search: "30-60-90-template").
- Manager review form: submit via People Ops Intake (link: /people-ops/intake).
- New hire Slack announcement template: short paragraph with role, start date, and 1-line ask.

## Measurement and Continuous Improvement
We track four operational metrics for onboarding quality: time-to-first-commit, time-to-merge-for-first-feature, new-hire Net Promoter Score (nhNPS) at day 30/90, and first-90 retention. Quarterly reviews of these metrics drive improvements to the playbook.
